name: Judas Jude
overview: The Scriptures reveal multiple individuals named Judas or Jude, each with distinct roles in the New Testament narrative. Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve apostles, is notably identified as the betrayer of Jesus, as Jesus foretold during the Last Supper, and as the one who conspired with the chief priests, receiving thirty pieces of silver as payment (Matthew 10:4; 26:14, 21; Zechariah 11:12-13). Another Judas is mentioned as a physical brother of Jesus, highlighting the familial ties within Christ's earthly life (Matthew 13:55). These references emphasize both the human relationships around Jesus and the tragic betrayal that led to His crucifixion.
